frozen: 2026-11-05, before any holdout coding; changes after this date are amendments and must be logged in SPEC_STUDY3.md
material: discovery half only (data/study3/qual_discovery.json); holdout = data/study3/qual_holdout.json, coded once

party_values.JEWISH_ISRAELI: Jews as a people or community; Israel, its government, forces, citizens; the Zionist movement and its organisations; the Yishuv and pre-state Jewish militias; Hebrew / Jewish-tradition names.
party_values.PALESTINIAN_ARAB: Palestinians and Palestinian organisations (PLO, Hamas, PA, militias); Arab states and forces in the Arab-Israeli context; Arabic / Islamic names of places and shared holy sites in Israel-Palestine.
party_values.OTHER_STATE: Any other state, government, empire or ruling power (e.g. Turkey, China, the Ottoman government, Britain).
party_values.OTHER_GROUP: Any other people, community, movement or non-state armed group (e.g. Uyghurs, Kurds, the TPLF, Al-Shabaab).
party_values.MULTIPLE: The move applies to two or more parties at once and cannot be split.
party_values.UNCLEAR: Party cannot be determined from the text.

coding_set: topic pairs (group == treatment) with change > 0.05, plus all comparison pairs (control, control_contaminated); pairs flagged parse_artefact by auto_kpis are excluded

length_strata.derived_from: exact terciles (158.3, 340.7) of the discovery coding set before the artefact exclusion (n = 213), rounded down

decision_rule.pair_score: LLM KPI: mean of the two coders' binary primary indicators (0, 0.5, 1) after orientation is restored and non-verbatim evidence is voided; auto KPI: its 0/1 field
decision_rule.estimate: Delta = mean pair score in topic minus mean pair score in comparison
decision_rule.ci: 95% percentile bootstrap, 10,000 resamples of pairs within group, seed 20261105
decision_rule.p: two-sided permutation p, 10,000 label permutations, seed 20261105 (used instead of a CI-derived p because several comparison cells are 0, which makes bootstrap p degenerate)
decision_rule.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10 across the 6 primaries (family fixed regardless of reliability); separately across the 6 secondaries (exploratory)
decision_rule.length: Mantel-Haenszel risk difference across the 3 lead0 terciles, weights n_t*n_c/(n_t+n_c); 95% CI by bootstrap within group x tercile; p by permuting group labels within tercile

verdicts.unreliable: LLM KPI with Cohen's kappa (binary primary indicator) < 0.6, or no variance: reported, not interpreted
verdicts.supported: reliable AND BH-adjusted q <= 0.10 AND Delta > 0 AND MH risk difference > 0 with stratified permutation p <= 0.10
verdicts.length_sensitive: BH-significant with Delta > 0 but the MH condition fails

sensitivity: coder combination AND (both positive) and OR (either positive)
comparison restricted to change > 0.05 (same filter as topic)
excluding pairs either coder marked usable = false
decision_rule.direction_breakdown: for every KPI, share of pairs with each (party, dir) instance, by group; descriptive, no tests

reliability.coders: two independent LLM coding sessions, no shared context, same prompt (coder_instructions.md), independent A/B orientation and item order
reliability.statistic: Cohen's kappa per KPI on the binary primary indicator (threshold 0.6) and on the full categorical code (reported); raw agreement, PABAK and prevalence reported
reliability.evidence_rule: a positive code whose evidence is not a verbatim substring of the cited version is set to none for that coder; if more than 15% of a coder's positive codes fail, that coder is re-run once in a fresh session and both runs are reported
reliability.auto: deterministic; validity checks: K04a vs LLM K04 colonial subset (kappa), K09 span precision audit

masking.coder_sees: cleaned lead texts as Version A and Version B in random order (independent per coder), plus an unordered list of other first-sentence variants from traced edits (text only), where available
masking.coder_does_not_see: title, group label, dates, edit summaries, timestamps, revert flags, which version is older
masking.order_key: KEY_DO_NOT_SHARE.json written by make_batches.py, used only by analyze_codes.py
limits: The content usually reveals the subject, and so whether it is a topic article; masking guards against knowing the group label and the before/after direction, not the subject.
Party codes name Jewish/Israeli and Palestinian/Arab parties explicitly, so the coder knows what the study is about.
First-sentence variants exist for 17 topic and 7 comparison discovery articles, mostly heavily edited ones; their presence weakly signals salience.

kpis.name: voice_upgrade
sources: voice:M1 Voice promotion of legal/atrocity categories
history:M6 Voice hardening of contested labels

reader_counts.voice: 8/85 topic (3 reverse) vs 0/37 comparison (legal/atrocity categories); consensus quantifier 11/85 vs 3/37

kpis.question: Does a contested characterisation that appears in both versions sit on a different rung of the attribution ladder in B than in A?
kpis.unit: lead pair (instances: one per aligned characterisation)

ladder.0: absent (only for the secondary readout of new claims)
ladder.1: alleged / accused / claimed, or presented as a disputed allegation ('allegations have been made', 'has been accused of')
ladder.2: attributed to an unquantified minority, to 'some', to critics, or to one party ('some historians', 'critics call', 'Palestinians describe')
ladder.3: attributed to named authorities or institutions ('according to the UN', 'the ICJ found', 'the international community considers')
ladder.4: majority or consensus attribution ('many scholars', 'most experts', 'scholars widely', 'academic consensus')
ladder.5: narrator voice: main-clause assertion with no attribution, or part of the definitional predicate

kpis.rule: List each contested characterisation (an evaluative, legal or atrocity category, or an intent/historicity claim) applied to the same target in BOTH versions. Assign its ladder rung in A and in B. Code B_more_narrator if at least one characterisation is on a higher rung in B and none lower; B_less_narrator if at least one is lower and none higher; both if each occurs; none otherwise.
include: Categories: genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal/unlawful/violation of international law, war crimes, crimes against humanity, terrorism/terrorist, massacre, colonial/settler-colonial, racism, antisemitism, propaganda; historicity claims (whether X existed or happened); intent claims ('intended to', 'aimed at').
Same category and same target in both versions, rungs differ by at least one step.
Upgrades and downgrades, for any target, in either group.
exclude: Rewording on the same rung ('accused' to 'charged'); swapping one named authority for another (3 to 3).
A characterisation present in only one version (record it as an instance with level 0 on the absent side; it does NOT set the code).
Casualty numbers, dates and other descriptive facts.
Words inside a quotation of a named person when the quotation is the only carrier.

direction_labels.B_more_narrator: moves a characterisation of [party]'s conduct or nature from attributed/hedged toward narrator voice
direction_labels.B_less_narrator: moves a characterisation of [party]'s conduct or nature from narrator voice toward attributed/hedged

sources: voice:M9 Narrative onset and first-paragraph primacy

reader_counts.history: 11/71 vs 3/20 (sub-type 'origin moved to a single originating agent' 7/71 vs 0/20)

kpis.question: Does B start the causal story of the subject earlier than A, or add an earlier prior cause or precondition, compared with A?
kpis.rule: In each version find the earliest event or condition that the lead presents as the origin, cause or precondition of the subject (cues: 'has its origins in', 'began', 'dates (back) to', 'rooted in', 'marked the start', 'arose from', 'after', 'following', 'in response to', 'as a reaction to', or a premodifier that encodes a precondition at the start of the event, e.g. 'from the blockaded Gaza Strip'). B_earlier: B's earliest stated cause is earlier in time than A's, or B adds a prior cause or precondition before the event A presented as the start. B_later: B removes the earlier origin or prior cause, or starts the causal story later. both: one chain moves earlier and another later.
include: Explicit causal or origin connectors, and precondition premodifiers attached to the starting event.
A prior cause that is an action of any party, or a condition (e.g. a constitution, a coup, a blockade).
exclude: Chronology without a causal link (founding dates, lists of later wars, updates to recent events).
Background about the subject itself that is not presented as a cause.
Consequences (what followed).
The same origin with the same anchor in both versions, even if reworded.

instance_fields.party: party whose action (or condition it imposed) is the added/removed earliest cause; UNCLEAR if a condition with no actor

direction_labels.B_earlier: moves the start of the causal story earlier, to an action or condition of [party]
direction_labels.B_later: moves the start of the causal story later / removes [party]'s earlier action as a cause

kpis.name: name_primacy
sources: voice:M10 Primary-referent naming and co-name order
history:M9 Toponymic and temporal anachronism management
kpis.question: Does B change which name is primary for the subject or for a place, territory or polity it mentions, or the status or order of alternative names associated with different communities?
kpis.unit: lead pair (flag whether the change is in the first sentence)
kpis.rule: Code changed when, for the SAME referent, B (a) uses a different name as head or primary name; (b) adds or removes an alternative name associated with another community, language or tradition; (c) reorders co-names or moves a name between primary status ('X or Y', bold co-name) and gloss status ('known to Muslims as Y', 'in Jewish tradition', '(roughly corresponding to Y)'); or (d) replaces the name used for an earlier period with another name for the same period (e.g. 'southern Syrian provinces' vs 'region of Palestine' vs 'Land of Israel').
include: Head-noun toponym swaps, gloss added/removed, co-name order, period-name replacement; anywhere in the lead (most occur in paragraph 1).
exclude: Transliteration, diacritics, script, pronunciation fixes.
Macro-region labels for a present-day location (Middle East / West Asia / Western Asia / Levant / Southern Levant): general style, do NOT code.
Administrative modifiers ('currently governed as part of X').
Labels for actors (code K05) and names inside quotations.
A name that disappears only because the sentence about its referent was deleted entirely.

instance_fields.party: community whose name is promoted or demoted

direction_labels.B_promotes: moves the name used by [party]'s tradition into primary position (head noun, first, or co-primary)
direction_labels.B_demotes: moves the name used by [party]'s tradition into a gloss, later position, or out of the lead

kpis.question: Does the defining predicate of the first sentence gain (or lose) a colonial, atrocity, legal-violation or apartheid/racism category in narrator voice?
kpis.rule: Take the defining predicate of the first sentence: the head noun phrase of 'X is/was a ...' (or 'X refers to', 'X was the ... of'), its modifiers, and its means or purpose adjunct ('through colonization'). B_gains: B's predicate contains a category from the four classes in narrator voice and A's does not (or has it only attributed). B_loses: the reverse. both: one class gained and another lost. Classes: colonial (colonization, colonies, colonial, settler-colonial); atrocity (genocide, ethnic cleansing, massacre, mass murder, mass expulsion, extermination); legal violation (illegal, unlawful, in violation of international law, war crimes); apartheid/racism (apartheid, racist, supremacist).
include: Category in the defining predicate or its adjunct, stated without an attribution frame.
Alternative names that carry the category ('also called Israeli colonies').
exclude: Category inside an attribution frame within the first sentence ('has been described as a form of settler colonialism').
Category outside the first sentence (K01/K06 may apply).
Same class in both versions (e.g. 'The Armenian genocide was the systematic destruction ...' in both).
Changes into or out of militant/terrorist/nationalist/political classes: that is style control SC1, not K04.
'ethnic nationalist' and other nationalism subtypes.

instance_fields.party: party whose conduct or nature the category characterises

direction_labels.B_gains: moves the definition of [party]'s project/act into a colonial / atrocity / legal-violation / apartheid class in narrator voice
direction_labels.B_loses: removes such a class from the definition of [party]'s project/act

kpis.question: Does B change the category of the label for a collective actor that is present in both versions, and in particular move it to an ideological label?
kpis.rule: Label categories: E ethnoreligious or national people ('Jewish militias', 'the Jewish population', 'Arab forces', 'Turks'); S state ('Israel', 'IDF', 'Israeli forces', 'the Ottoman government'); I ideological or movement ('Zionists', 'Zionist militants', 'Islamists', 'jihadists', 'Kemalists'); O named organisation ('Irgun', 'Haganah', 'Hamas', 'the CUP'). For the same real-world actor in both versions: B_more_ideological if B uses I where A used E, S or O; B_less_ideological if the reverse; other_change if the category changes without involving I; both if I is gained for one actor and lost for another.
include: The subject's own genus when it names a collective actor ('paramilitary organization of the Jewish population' -> 'Zionist paramilitary organization').
Actors in by-phrases, subjects and premodifiers.
exclude: The ideology as an idea or its proper name ('Zionism', 'the Zionist movement', 'Islamism').
Self-designations in quotation.
An actor mentioned in only one version (the scope of who did harm is K07).
Same-category synonyms ('Israel' -> 'the IDF' is S -> S).

reader_counts.history: 9/71 vs 0/20 (deleted 4, motive added 1, kept after a prior cause 3, newly added as trigger 2)

kpis.question: Does B change the narrative role of a party's refusal, rejection or first attack that A presented as the trigger of a war, a displacement or a failed settlement?
kpis.rule: B_recontextualises: in B that refusal or first act is (a) deleted, (b) given a stated motive or reason, or (c) preceded in the same paragraph by an earlier cause attributed to another party. B_reinstates: the reverse (added as an unexplained trigger, motive removed, prior cause removed). both / none.
include: Rejection of partition or peace plans or conditions; an invasion or attack presented as starting a war; evacuation orders or voluntary departure presented as a cause of flight; refusal to recognise.
exclude: Refusals that are not presented as a trigger or cause; unchanged role; pure relocation within the lead without change of role.

direction_labels.B_recontextualises: moves [party]'s refusal/first act from inciting cause to a response with reasons, or out of the lead
direction_labels.B_reinstates: moves [party]'s refusal/first act into the role of unexplained trigger

kpis.question: Does B add, strengthen, remove or re-attribute a claim that grounds a group's tie to a land?
kpis.unit: lead pair (instances: one per group x claim type)
kpis.rule: Claim types: continuity (ancestral homeland, return, re-establishment, birthplace, persisting presence, ancient polity as the group's own); demography (the group as historical majority or minority, percentages, 'since at least the 12th century'); indigeneity ('indigenous', 'native' applied to a group). B_strengthens: claim added, or moved toward narrator voice / de-hedged. B_weakens: deleted, or moved into a party's voice ('Zionists viewed ...') / hedged. both / none.
include: Any group, in either group of articles.
exclude: Present-day population statistics with no historical frame; diaspora history that is not about the tie to the land; unchanged claims.

direction_labels.B_strengthens: strengthens [party]'s stated tie to the land (by type)
direction_labels.B_weakens: removes or re-attributes [party]'s stated tie to the land (by type)

kpis.question: Does B newly present harm suffered by a group as the motive or cause of that same group's later action?
kpis.rule: B_adds_motive: B adds or makes explicit a causal link from harm or grievance suffered by group X (pogroms, genocide, persecution, expulsion, discrimination, occupation) to an action by group X (migration, organising, armed struggle, state-building), via 'fleeing', 'stimulated by', 'in response to', 'as a reaction to', 'driven by'. exclude: Harm presented as the consequence of another party's act (consequence slot); casualty updates; harm mentioned with no causal link to the group's own action.
